title: Practice habits and how Punch got into the plantation band
summary: Punch tells of an hour's practice a day and moving from drum to valve trombone, baritone and cornet in the band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Okay. How long did you practice when you first took up trumpet fire?
How long did you practice? Who horn?
Yeah. How long did you practice horn?
Oh, well, I say when I first picked up, we must have went for something around a year before we got to doing any good.
Yeah, but I mean a day. How many hours a day would you practice?

Oh, well, when I first picked up horn, I wouldn't have, but no time to practice at 12 o'clock in the day when I come from work. Uh-huh. Practice at 12 o'clock in the day and again at night when I get off, see? Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And on Sundays when we get on the corners, they call it, everybody had a horn blowing.
Well, how long would you practice at night?
At night? Couldn't practice long, man. Maybe about an hour. I could put them horn down and go to bed.
Uh-huh. I see. Well, that's just the opposite of the way it is now.

Yeah, you see, how I got to London, everybody was with me. Them older men on the place had bands, see? Uh-huh. Well, they got all the new instruments and anybody that had any relation to give the old instrument to them, see? But me, I had nobody in the band. None of my people was in the band. But I just got in there with the boys, you know, and started to train the drum. Got off the drum, got on the val trombone. Then I got on the baritone. Next thing I was on the trumpet. Cornette, they called them then. And from then on, I just started blowing, you know, went on to the army, come to the army, and I did all right.
